implementation_notes: Kotlin collapses the envelope into a data class plus the serialization plugin: a generic @Serializable data class with an explicit headers map and the payload as type parameter replaces the classic wrapper, and kotlinx.serialization supplies the wire form (JSON, CBOR or protobuf). On the transport side client APIs already expose metadata (Ktor HttpHeaders, AMQP client properties), so a body envelope is only needed when the channel carries nothing. Keep the classic hand-written wrapper only for a byte-exact legacy format.
pitfalls: Generic serializers must be passed explicitly (Envelope.serializer(Order.serializer())); a missing one fails at runtime in reflective call paths rather than at compile time.
kotlinx.serialization rejects unknown keys by default: an envelope field added by a newer producer breaks older consumers unless the reader sets ignoreUnknownKeys.
Payload nullability and default values are part of the wire contract: a non-null field without a default makes the envelope undecodable for messages from older producers.
